title: 'Book Review': Robert Caro on 50 Years of 'The Power Broker'

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Hey everyone, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: As you might have noticed, we're putting something different down our feed today.
sentences.zh: 正如你们可能注意到的，我们今天在节目推送中发布了一些不同的内容。

sentences.en: It's a recent episode of our New York Times podcast about books hosted by Gilbert Cruz.
sentences.zh: 这是我们《纽约时报》书评播客最近的一期节目，由吉尔伯特·克鲁兹主持。

sentences.en: In this particular episode, Gilbert speaks with the writer Robert Caro.
sentences.zh: 在这一期节目中，吉尔伯特采访了作家罗伯特·卡罗。

sentences.en: About his seminal, renowned non-fiction book, The Power Broker, which is now 50 years old.
sentences.zh: 谈论他那本具有开创性、享誉盛名的非虚构作品《权力掮客》，该书出版至今已有50年了。

sentences.en: If you haven't read it, and there's no reason to be embarrassed if you haven't, it's the story of Robert Moses, who shaped New York City.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没读过——没读过也没什么好尴尬的——它是关于罗伯特·摩西的故事，正是他塑造了纽约市。

sentences.en: But as the many people who are obsessed with The Power Broker can tell you, it's a singular fable of politics and power in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但正如许多痴迷于《权力掮客》的人所说，这是一个关于美国政治与权力的独特寓言。

sentences.en: It's an incredible story and an incredible book.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不可思议的故事，也是一本不可思议的书。

sentences.en: Okay, here's Gilbert with Robert Caro on the New York Times Book Review podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 好了，下面是吉尔伯特与罗伯特·卡罗在《纽约时报》书评播客中的对话。

sentences.en: Take a listen.
sentences.zh: 请听。

sentences.en: I'm Gilbert Cruz, editor of the New York Times Book Review, and this is the Book Review PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》书评主编吉尔伯特·克鲁兹，这是书评播客。

sentences.en: This week, I'm joined by a modern master of biography and history writing, Mr. Robert Caro.
sentences.zh: 本周，我邀请到了一位传记与历史写作的现代大师，罗伯特·卡罗先生。

sentences.en: He has written four volumes of The Years of Lyndon Johnson, a multi-book work on the life of the 36th President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了四卷本的《林登·约翰逊传》，这是一部关于美国第36任总统生平的多卷本巨著。

sentences.en: Volume 3, Master of the Senate, won the Pulitzer Prize.
sentences.zh: 第三卷《参议院的主人》获得了普利策奖。

sentences.en: Volume 4, Passage of Power, appeared on our recent list of the best books of the 21st century so far.
sentences.zh: 第四卷《权力的通道》出现在我们最近评选的21世纪至今最佳图书榜单上。

sentences.en: Before all that, however, in September 1974, 50 years ago, he published The Power Broker, a book about the man who built modern New York City, Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 然而在此之前，即50年前的1974年9月，他出版了《权力掮客》，这本书讲述了建造现代纽约市的人——罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: Robert Moses built beaches and parkways.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西建造了海滩和公园大道。

sentences.en: He built bridges and expressways.
sentences.zh: 他建造了桥梁和高速公路。

sentences.en: He built Lincoln Center and Shea Stadium and the United Nations headquarters.
sentences.zh: 他建造了林肯中心、谢伊体育场和联合国总部。

sentences.en: Robert Caro built The Power Broker, a book both titanic in length and scope, and one that continues to be read and discussed and obsessed over to this very day.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·卡罗建造了《权力掮客》，这是一本在篇幅和广度上都堪称宏大的书，至今仍被人们阅读、讨论和痴迷。

sentences.en: Robert Caro, welcome back to the Book Review PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·卡罗，欢迎回到书评播客。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Now, Mr. Caro, and I'm going to call you Bob because we just discussed what I should call you, I don't want to necessarily go through a summary of the book.
sentences.zh: 卡罗先生——我还是叫你鲍勃吧，因为我们刚才讨论过该怎么称呼你——我不想单纯地回顾这本书的内容。

sentences.en: I want to go through a summary of who Robert Moses is.
sentences.zh: 我想回顾一下罗伯特·摩西到底是个什么样的人。

sentences.en: I think if people are listening to this interview, they've read it, or maybe they've seen the documentary Turn Every Page from a few years ago about you and Bob Gottlieb.
sentences.zh: 我想如果人们在听这次采访，他们应该已经读过这本书，或者看过几年前关于你和鲍勃·戈特利布的纪录片《翻过每一页》。

sentences.en: Hopefully, I'm not going to ask you to say things about Robert Moses that you've been saying for the past half century,
sentences.zh: 希望我不会要求你再说出那些你过去半个世纪一直在说的话，

sentences.en: but 50 years is significant.
sentences.zh: 但50年是一个重要的节点。

sentences.en: I would argue that nonfiction, biography, history, a lot of it doesn't stand the test of time in that way.
sentences.zh: 我认为非虚构作品、传记和历史类书籍中，很多都经不起时间的考验。

sentences.en: But The Power Broker has.
sentences.zh: 但《权力掮客》做到了。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering why you think it has lasted as this own monument in its way for so long, 50 years.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为它为什么能像一座纪念碑一样屹立这么久，整整50年。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I know the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 我不确定自己是否知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: I've been thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I think people are interested in power.
sentences.zh: 我想人们对权力很感兴趣。

sentences.en: This is a particular kind of power.
sentences.zh: 这是一种特殊的权力。

sentences.en: Robert Moses' power was unchecked power.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西的权力是不受制约的权力。

sentences.en: We all live in a democracy where we think that power comes from our votes at the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 我们都生活在民主社会，认为权力来自我们在投票箱前的选票。

sentences.en: Here was a man who was never elected to anything, and he held on to power for 44 years, almost half a century.
sentences.zh: 而这个人从未当选过任何职位，却掌握了44年的权力，几乎半个世纪。

sentences.en: And with the power, this man who wasn't elected to anything shaped New York and its surrounding suburbs.
sentences.zh: 凭借这种权力，这个从未当选过任何职位的人塑造了纽约及其周边郊区。

sentences.en: So I think if you're interested in government, you have to say, as I said, maybe 55 years ago when I started this, how did he do it?
sentences.zh: 所以我想如果你对政府感兴趣，你必须像我大约55年前开始写这本书时那样问：他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: What happened here?
sentences.zh: 这里发生了什么？

sentences.en: No one even, I have to say, when I started this book, I don't think there was any real awareness, even among mayors and council members and governors,
sentences.zh: 甚至没有人——我必须说，当我开始写这本书时，我认为即使在市长、议员和州长中间，也没有真正的意识，

sentences.en: of where this power came from.
sentences.zh: 意识到这种权力来自哪里。

sentences.en: Do you have a sense, this book, being 50 years old, that people that go into government read it and have read it?
sentences.zh: 你是否感觉到，这本书出版50年了，那些进入政府工作的人读过它吗？

sentences.en: I know that many journalists pick it up early in their careers because it is such a sort of impressive achievement in reporting and writing.
sentences.zh: 我知道许多记者在职业生涯早期就会读它，因为它在报道和写作方面确实是一项令人印象深刻的成就。

sentences.en: But when it comes to people in government, do you talk to congresspeople and senators and state representatives who say,
sentences.zh: 但当谈到政府官员时，你会和国会议员、参议员和州代表交谈，他们会说，

sentences.en: I've read The Power Broker when I was 25?
sentences.zh: 我在25岁时读过《权力掮客》吗？

sentences.en: Yes, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 是的，说实话。

sentences.en: And what is their takeaway?
sentences.zh: 他们的收获是什么？

sentences.en: They're very complimentary about it.
sentences.zh: 他们对这本书评价很高。

sentences.en: I think over and over, I hear people say, you're making me say boastful things.
sentences.zh: 我想我一遍又一遍地听到人们说——你让我说这些自夸的话——

sentences.en: I've never read anything like it.
sentences.zh: 我从未读过像这样的书。

sentences.en: You've explained to me where power comes from, a particular kind of power.
sentences.zh: 你向我解释了权力来自哪里，一种特殊的权力。

sentences.en: Now I say that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 现在我常说这种话。

sentences.en: Of course, very wonderful to me to hear it.
sentences.zh: 当然，听到这些对我来说非常美妙。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of the things that I learned in the book still hold very true today.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我在书中了解到的许多事情在今天依然非常适用。

sentences.en: You have written so much about power, whether it's in this book or over the many volumes of your Lyndon Johnson biography, and said in a Paris Review interview the following.
sentences.zh: 你写了很多关于权力的内容，无论是在这本书里，还是在你那多卷本的林登·约翰逊传记中，并且在《巴黎评论》的一次采访中说了以下内容。

sentences.en: And I just, I love the way you put it.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢你的表达方式。

sentences.en: And I'd love for you to comment upon it further if you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你能进一步评论一下，我会很高兴。

sentences.en: You said power doesn't always corrupt.
sentences.zh: 你说权力并不总是腐蚀人。

sentences.en: And you can see it in the case of, for example, Al Smith or Sam Rayburn.
sentences.zh: 你可以从阿尔·史密斯或萨姆·雷伯恩的例子中看到这一点。

sentences.en: There, power cleanses.
sentences.zh: 在那里，权力是净化剂。

sentences.en: But what power always does is reveal.
sentences.zh: 但权力总是能揭示真相。

sentences.en: Talk to me a little bit more about that.
sentences.zh: 再多跟我谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: When you're trying to get power, when you're climbing toward power, maybe there are things in you or ways that you're acting or to get power,
sentences.zh: 当你试图获取权力，当你攀登权力巅峰时，也许你身上有一些东西，或者你为了获得权力而采取的行为方式，

sentences.en: that if people knew about them, they would be turned off on you or they'd be afraid of you.
sentences.zh: 如果人们知道了，他们会反感你，或者会害怕你。

sentences.en: But once you get the power, once you have it, then you can act or do whatever you intended to do all along.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你获得了权力，一旦你拥有了它，你就可以按照你一直打算做的方式去行动或行事。

sentences.en: A really good example of that is Lyndon Johnson, who for 20 years voted with the South on every civil rights bill.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是林登·约翰逊，他在20年里对每一项民权法案都投了支持南方的票。

sentences.en: Even, he even voted against the bill that would have made lynching a federal crime.
sentences.zh: 甚至，他甚至投票反对将私刑定为联邦罪行的法案。

sentences.en: And then he becomes president.
sentences.zh: 然后他成为了总统。

sentences.en: President Kennedy is assassinated.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪总统遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: And he has to give a speech to Congress four days later.
sentences.zh: 四天后他必须向国会发表讲话。

sentences.en: And he's not even in the Oval Office yet.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还没搬进椭圆形办公室。

sentences.en: He's still living down in Spring Valley.
sentences.zh: 他仍然住在春谷。

sentences.en: And he's going to bed.
sentences.zh: 他正准备睡觉。

sentences.en: And downstairs, there are four of his speechwriters, his aides, working on the speech that he has to give to Congress and reveal what kind of president he's going to be.
sentences.zh: 楼下，他的四位演讲稿撰写人、他的助手们，正在为他向国会发表的演讲工作，以揭示他将成为什么样的总统。

sentences.en: And he comes down and he says, basically, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 他走下楼说，基本上，你们做得怎么样了？

sentences.en: And they say, we're still not doing very well.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们做得还是不太好。

sentences.en: But one thing we are all agreed on, don't make a priority out of civil rights.
sentences.zh: 但有一点我们都同意，不要把民权作为优先事项。

sentences.en: If you do that, the Southern senators who have the power in the Senate will do the same thing to you that they did to Kennedy and stop your entire congressional.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，在参议院拥有权力的南方参议员们会对你做同样的事，就像他们对肯尼迪做的那样，阻止你所有的国会提案。

sentences.en: And they say, it's a noble cause, one of them says.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人说，这是一个崇高的事业。

sentences.en: But it's not a cause that you should fight for.
sentences.zh: 但这不是你应该去争取的事业。

sentences.en: And Lyndon Johnson says, what's a presidency for then?
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊说，那总统职位是为了什么？

sentences.en: And in the speech, he says, our first priority should be to pass Jack Kennedy's civil rights bill.
sentences.zh: 在演讲中，他说，我们的首要任务应该是通过杰克·肯尼迪的民权法案。

sentences.en: And you say, if the Southern senators had for all those years knew how he felt, they would not have raised him to power.
sentences.zh: 你说，如果南方参议员们多年来都知道他的真实想法，他们就不会把他推上权力宝座。

sentences.en: So it's really, in a way, I hope, a perfect example of what you asked me for.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，我希望这正是你所要求的完美例子。

sentences.en: Is it possible to rise to power, at least in our system of democracy, without that sort of veiled part of you, that shadow part of you, where you know some things that you believe,
sentences.zh: 是否有可能在不展现那种隐秘的、阴暗的一面的情况下获得权力——至少在我们的民主体制下——在那里你知道一些你所相信的事情，

sentences.en: but you know that if you tell people too loudly that you'll never get what you want, which is to be in charge?
sentences.zh: 但你知道如果你大声告诉人们，你就永远无法得到你想要的，也就是掌权？

sentences.en: It's a terrific question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的问题。

sentences.en: And I can't answer it for, in the large sense, for everybody.
sentences.zh: 我无法从宏观意义上为每个人回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I know with Lyndon Johnson, it was absolutely necessary just to go in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我知道对于林登·约翰逊来说，这对于进入参议院是绝对必要的。

sentences.en: When he comes to the Senate, well, I forget the year, but this is approximately right.
sentences.zh: 当他来到参议院时，嗯，我忘了年份，但大致是这样。

sentences.en: There are 17 great standing committees of the Senate, and Southern is the chairman of 11 of them.
sentences.zh: 参议院有17个重要的常设委员会，南方人担任其中11个委员会的主席。

sentences.en: They have the power.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握着权力。

sentences.en: If they don't like you, you are not going anywhere in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不喜欢你，你在参议院就寸步难行。

sentences.en: And he wants to rise to power in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他想在参议院崛起。

sentences.en: He cannot let them know.
sentences.zh: 他不能让他们知道（他的真实想法）。

sentences.en: And he's a genius at concealing himself.
sentences.zh: 他是一个隐藏自己的天才。

sentences.en: And if you want to know just how much of a genius he is in this regard, the leader of the South is Richard Russell.
sentences.zh: 如果你想知道他在这一方面有多天才，南方势力的领袖是理查德·拉塞尔。

sentences.en: Russell, there are chapters called, the Russell of the Russells of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔，有几章专门写了乔治亚州的拉塞尔家族。

sentences.en: They are a ruling family.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个统治家族。

sentences.en: And he asks, the secretary of the Senate is a guy named Bobby Baker.
sentences.zh: 他问参议院秘书，一个叫鲍比·贝克的人。

sentences.en: He says, everybody else who comes to the Senate asks, what are the rules?
sentences.zh: 他说，其他来到参议院的人都会问，规则是什么？

sentences.en: Where do you sit?
sentences.zh: 我坐在哪里？

sentences.en: Lyndon Johnson only asked one question.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊只问了一个问题。

sentences.en: Who has the power here?
sentences.zh: 谁在这里掌握权力？

sentences.en: I had no trouble.
sentences.zh: 我毫不费力。

sentences.en: I said, Richard Russell.
sentences.zh: 我说，理查德·拉塞尔。

sentences.en: Johnson doesn't ask for an important committee.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊没有要求进入重要的委员会。

sentences.en: He says, what's Russell's committee?
sentences.zh: 他说，拉塞尔的委员会是什么？

sentences.en: He's chairman of armed services.
sentences.zh: 他是武装部队委员会的主席。

sentences.en: Lyndon Johnson says, I'd like to be on armed services, because he knows that's the only way he can spend a lot of time with Richard Russell.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊说，我想加入武装部队委员会，因为他知道那是他能花大量时间与理查德·拉塞尔在一起的唯一途径。

sentences.en: He starts to stay late at the Senate because Russell is a bachelor, a very lonely man.
sentences.zh: 他开始在参议院待到很晚，因为拉塞尔是个单身汉，一个非常孤独的人。

sentences.en: And he stays late working.
sentences.zh: 他工作到很晚。

sentences.en: Now, Lyndon Johnson stays working with him.
sentences.zh: 现在，林登·约翰逊留下来和他一起工作。

sentences.en: Richard Russell gets a hamburger late at night before he goes home.
sentences.zh: 理查德·拉塞尔在回家前深夜吃个汉堡。

sentences.en: Lyndon Johnson gets a hamburger with him.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊就和他一起吃汉堡。

sentences.en: And Sunday breakfast, he invites Richard Russell over, or Sunday brunch more.
sentences.zh: 周日早餐，他邀请理查德·拉塞尔过来，或者说是周日早午餐。

sentences.en: He has two little girls.
sentences.zh: 他有两个小女儿。

sentences.en: Russell is very wonderful with little children.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔对小孩子非常好。

sentences.en: He loves them.
sentences.zh: 他爱她们。

sentences.en: They love him.
sentences.zh: 她们也爱他。

sentences.en: And soon they are very close.
sentences.zh: 很快他们就变得非常亲密。

sentences.en: So Richard Russell is sitting there right in front of Lyndon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 所以理查德·拉塞尔就坐在林登·约翰逊面前。

sentences.en: When he's become president, and Lyndon Johnson says, our first priority has to become civil rights.

sentences.zh: 你有一个每天都要去上班的办公室。

sentences.zh: 你穿上西装，打上领带，去你那个一成不变的办公室。

sentences.en: Oh, I thought about that a lot because I used to have an office there, and I used to look down on the Coliseum, and I used to remember that Robert Moses used to say,

sentences.zh: 我的作品将成就我，

sentences.en: And I think he is, in a way, by the sheer number of works.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在某种程度上，他确实做到了，就凭他作品的数量之多。

sentences.en: Some of them will come down, you know, the Coliseum.
sentences.zh: 其中一些会被拆除，你知道的，比如体育馆。

sentences.en: Oh, he was responsible.
sentences.zh: 哦，他是负责人。

sentences.en: Okay, did Shea Stadium no longer exist?
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢伊体育场也不存在了吗？

sentences.en: There are maybe a couple of other ones, but by and large, the things, the lines that he etched into a piece of paper are still there.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他几个，但总的来说，他在纸上勾勒出的那些线条依然存在。

sentences.en: And for all I know, they'll be there forever.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它们将永远存在。

sentences.zh: 那么，让我问你一个问题。

sentences.zh: 你住在纽约，你是纽约人。

sentences.zh: 写完这本书后，你现在明白了纽约市是如何运作的，部分原因就是这个男人所做的决定。

sentences.zh: 即使在写完《权力掮客》这么多年后，你会对自己说吗，

sentences.zh: 该死的罗伯特·摩西，为什么我非得在这里堵车，就因为你不想修建这条轻轨？

sentences.zh: 我从来没有这样说过。

sentences.zh: 但我确实曾让我的妻子感到厌烦，我说，你看到这些车了吗？

sentences.en: It didn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 本不必如此的。

sentences.zh: 你有一个记录得非常详尽的过程。

sentences.zh: 我想人们喜欢问你的过程，也喜欢和你谈论你的过程，因为它如此细致、可靠，而且显然它能带来好的作品。

sentences.en: It results in some of the best pieces of biography and history of the past half century.
sentences.zh: 它造就了过去半个世纪中一些最好的传记和历史作品。

sentences.zh: 但你认为作为一名作家，对过程的执着是怎么回事？

sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.zh: 每个人都问我，我在开始写作之前会列出整本书的大纲。

sentences.zh: 然后当我写到每一章时，我会非常详细地列出大纲。

sentences.zh: 然后我用手写。

sentences.zh: 然后我通常会有很多草稿。

sentences.en: But I don't, I don't use a computer in the writing.

sentences.en: Everybody thinks it's, aren't you slow?

sentences.en: Couldn't you be faster?
sentences.zh: 你不能快点吗？

sentences.en: For me, it's more important to be slow.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，慢一点更重要。

sentences.en: And it's not a, it's not a blessing or anything I'm proud of.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么福气，也不是我引以为傲的事情。

sentences.en: I just learned the hard way that things go better for me if I do it slowly.
sentences.zh: 我只是吃一堑长一智，发现如果我慢慢来，事情会进展得更顺利。

sentences.en: I can understand that because everyone has to find their own way of writing.

sentences.zh: 我在用手思考。

sentences.zh: 这就是想法、联系、特定的词汇和过渡句来到我脑海中的方式。

sentences.en: They can't explain why.

sentences.en: But that's just the way that it works.
sentences.zh: 但这就是它的工作方式。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I imagine that's true for you?
sentences.zh: 我想这对你来说也是一样的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 你知道，当时的《新闻日报》有五个版本，因为他们有东部版、中萨福克版。

sentences.zh: 那是怎么回事？

sentences.zh: 你必须弄清楚

sentences.zh: 他是如何获得这种权力的？

sentences.en: That wasn't something that you learned.
sentences.zh: 这不是你通过学习就能知道的。

sentences.zh: 渐渐地，人们给了你关于创建公共机构的暗示。

sentences.zh: 我记得我当时想，

sentences.zh: 我不明白他在这个法案里做了什么。

sentences.zh: 我花了，我想那个法案，它非常长。
